target.title: refactor(ui): simplify Lit state ownership
target.body:
Closes #102821

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a Control UI ownership problem where the app host and shell copied values from already-subscribed gateway, navigation, overlay, config, theme, and agent capabilities into a second set of Lit state fields. Those parallel state paths added duplicate rendering and could drift as reconnect and capability behavior evolved.

Also fixes an issue where an already-open native-link menu kept labels from the previous locale after the active locale changed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The app and shell now render from the canonical capability snapshots while retaining only genuine local interaction state and required eager-load side effects. Repeated light-DOM `display: contents` setup now lives in one Lit base, and the native-link menu uses the locale-aware OpenClaw base.

The patch removes 136 production lines overall and does not change dependencies, configuration, persistence, public APIs, or visual layout.

## User Impact

Native-link actions retranslate immediately when the locale changes. Other Control UI behavior is intentionally unchanged, with fewer synchronization paths that can present stale shell state during future capability changes.

## Evidence

- Focused Control UI Vitest: 6 files, 17/17 tests passed.
- Focused browser E2E: 5 files, 11/11 scenarios passed, covering initial authentication, sidebar persistence and config gating, approvals, embedded terminal mode, and native-link routing.
- `pnpm check:changed`: passed type checks, core/UI lint, extension lint, and architecture/guard checks.
- `pnpm ui:build`: passed; 1,019 modules transformed.
- `git diff --check` and targeted Oxfmt checks: passed.
- Fresh pre-commit and committed-branch Codex autoreviews: no accepted/actionable findings.
- No screenshot attached because the change intentionally has no visual-layout delta; the locale transition is covered directly by the component regression.

AI-assisted: yes. The implementation was maintainer-directed, reviewed against the complete diff, and validated with focused unit/browser coverage plus repository gates.
